intro: Under $1,500 a month per person is the comfortable middle of the WashU (Washington University in St. Louis) market: enough for a solid place in a good location without luxury-tower pricing.

Every listing below qualifies on per-person cost, meaning your share after splitting the unit rent by bedrooms, or the room price where a listing rents by the room. At this budget you get a real choice between living alone in some areas or taking the nicer shared place. Walk times and student reviews are on every card.
directAnswer: Under $1,500 a month per person buys real choice near WashU: most shared 2 and 3 bedrooms qualify, and so do many 1 bedrooms in Skinker-DeBaliviere and University City, MO. Every listing on this page fits that budget per person.

faqs.q: Can I live alone near WashU for under $1,500?
faqs.a: Often, yes, especially in Skinker-DeBaliviere and University City, MO. Buildings right by campus can run higher, so check the actual listings and what utilities are included.

It’s calculated per person. A $2,800 two-bedroom works out to $1,400 per person if split evenly. Room-priced listings use the listed room price. Utilities vary, so check what’s included before comparing places.

faqs.q: What does this budget get me that cheaper places do not?
faqs.a: Mostly location and condition: shorter walks to campus, in-unit laundry, renovated kitchens, buildings with management that answers the phone. Whether a specific building delivers is what the student reviews on each listing are for.

faqs.q: When should I sign to get the best options at this budget?
faqs.a: Fall, for next August. Students report private landlords begin signing around November, and mid-range places in walkable blocks are the most competitive segment of the market. WashU affiliated companies open signing later in spring, so you get two waves of inventory.

benchmarkNote: Rents on this page are each listing's current asking rent. Proximity does not publish averages computed from its own listings.
